findings.problem: The revised driver path uses ubuntu-drivers install --gpgpu but the next X-configuration step assumes nvidia-xconfig is available. The retained Ubuntu driver guide lists the selected server NVIDIA utilities as an additional component; the manual provider identifies the utility package, so source support for the command syntax alone does not establish this clean-install prerequisite.
findings.required_change: Version the existing X-configuration lead-in to check nvidia-xconfig availability and install the NVIDIA utilities package matching the selected driver when necessary before running the following command. Preserve the exact current command, source scope and original packet; no runtime run or new passage scope is required.
findings.author_status: Author independently confirmed the gap and is preparing a versioned amendment.

substantive_acceptance_except_finding: The clean-host driver-selection correction uses current Ubuntu server/compute guidance without requiring a historical595-open result or promising current driver availability. Other nvidia-smi/Xid/NVML statements distinguish displayed information, supported fields and diagnostic possibilities from hardware or service-state guarantees.

The complete installer fallback now downloads its input, preserves opaque input, gates dependent operations and states device/port substitutions. Partition and format instructions retain explicit identity, disposable-target and successful-unmount prerequisites. No destructive command was executed.

APT corrections accurately distinguish configured candidates, dependency changes, held-back packages and target kernel metapackages. GA/HWE labels describe installed packages; the current running release and intended boot target remain separate.

GRUB corrections distinguish saved entries, menu indices, generated detection output and actual boot selection. They retain a previous-kernel recovery option and console access; no reboot-success guarantee is introduced.

The retained public send_mach_info.py source explicitly runs package/settings maintenance, component retrieval and fio operations in addition to submitting machine information. Its relative kaalia.log read supports the guarded subshell cwd correction. The installed script can differ, so its review and maintenance preconditions remain required.
The reset targets are the exact named paths in the independent original product guide. They remain scoped recovery instructions, without asserting a tested return to Online.
Source review does not demand fresh execution for command definitions, conditional advice or documented meanings. Existing operational and account limitations are retained.
review_limit: Independent read-only inspection of all literals/rationales, relevant complete page context and retained primary blocks, plus source/hash/selector and in-memory locality checks. Reused the author’s14 parse-only fence checks rather than rerunning them. No installation, service, storage, network, package, reboot, account, Git or graph operation was performed.
